```{python}
import pandas as pd
from loguru import logger

import _chart_theme as theme
from realtime import read_archive, revision_triangle

logger.disable("realtime")
archive = read_archive()

series_count = f"{archive['series_id'].nunique()}"
row_count = f"{len(archive):,}"
first_vintage_year = f"{archive['vintage_date'].min().year}"
latest_vintage = f"{archive['vintage_date'].max():%b %Y}"

EXAMPLE_QUARTER = pd.Period("2020Q2", "Q")
NOMINAL_GDP_SERIES = "YBHA"
PERCENT = 100
MILLIONS_PER_BILLION = 1_000

ihyq = archive.loc[archive["series_id"] == "IHYQ"].sort_values("vintage_date")
spring_2020 = ihyq.loc[ihyq["reference_period"] == EXAMPLE_QUARTER]
first_value = spring_2020["value"].iloc[0]
latest_value = spring_2020["value"].iloc[-1]
example_quarter = theme.quarter_in_words(EXAMPLE_QUARTER)
first_fall = f"{abs(first_value):.1f}"
latest_fall = f"{abs(latest_value):.1f}"
first_estimate_month = f"{spring_2020['vintage_date'].iloc[0]:%B %Y}"

quarterly_nominal_gdp = archive.loc[
    (archive["series_id"] == NOMINAL_GDP_SERIES) & (archive["frequency"] == "Q")
]
latest_nominal_gdp = revision_triangle(quarterly_nominal_gdp, NOMINAL_GDP_SERIES).iloc[-1].dropna()
latest_gdp_millions = latest_nominal_gdp.iloc[-1]
revision_points = abs(latest_value - first_value)
revision_billions = latest_gdp_millions * revision_points / PERCENT / MILLIONS_PER_BILLION
revision_points_text = f"{revision_points:.1f}"
revision_billions_text = f"{revision_billions:.1f}"
latest_gdp_billions_text = f"{latest_gdp_millions / MILLIONS_PER_BILLION:,.0f}"
latest_gdp_quarter = theme.quarter_in_words(latest_nominal_gdp.index[-1])
```

## Introduction

This is an archive of real-time data. It is inspired by [ALFRED](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/), the St. Louis Fed's archive of US data. We try to fill a similar gap for the UK. Coverage includes GDP and its main components, industry output, prices, the labour market, trade, household finances, government borrowing, and some survey data.

## Why a real-time data archive?

ONS first estimated that UK GDP fell by `{python} first_fall`% in the `{python} example_quarter`. That figure came out in `{python} first_estimate_month`. The estimate for the same quarter is now a fall of `{python} latest_fall`%. That difference of `{python} revision_points_text` percentage points would be equivalent to about £`{python} revision_billions_text` billion in a quarter today, based on the latest figure for quarterly GDP at current prices: £`{python} latest_gdp_billions_text` billion in the `{python} latest_gdp_quarter`. So... revisions matter!

Revisions matter for forecasting and nowcasting too. If we truly wish to know how our model will perform in real-time, we need real-time data!

## How are you providing the data?

As one file, in the super efficient and type-aware parquet format[^a], in one table. You can [download the file or query it directly](accessing_the_data.qmd). No account necessary!

Each row says: on this date, this value was published for this series and this period. Each row also records where the value came from and when it was downloaded, so you can trace any value back to the original file.

The [guide to the data](guide.qmd) explains more about what the archive holds, the decisions behind it and how far you can rely on it. Read it before using the figures in your own work.

[^a]: [Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/blog/what-is-parquet) estimate that it uses 87% less space than a CSV file, and can be read 34x faster.

## Citing the project

If you benefit from this "public good", we'd be really grateful if you could cite UK real time data. Citations help show that there's demand for this public good to be maintained, and for others to be created in the future.

The file is updated as new figures are published, so the citation gives the date of the latest publication it holds. Please cite the version you used:

```{python}
#| output: asis
latest_publication = archive["vintage_date"].max()
citation = f"""@misc{{turrell_uk_data,
  author = {{Turrell, Arthur}},
  title = {{{{UK}} Real-Time Data: What Was Published about the {{UK}} Economy, and When}},
  year = {{{latest_publication.year}}},
  url = {{https://aeturrell.github.io/real-time-data/}},
  note = {{Includes publications up to {latest_publication.day} {latest_publication:%B %Y}}}
}}"""
print(f"```bibtex\n{citation}\n```")
```
